subject: Milestone-tied commit schedule for dedicated capacity — Aurora Data
messages:
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Emily Park <emily@auroradata.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-12T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Milestone-tied commit schedule for dedicated capacity — Aurora Data

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time earlier this week. Per our conversation I wanted to put a concrete proposal on the table for a multi-year dedicated GPU+TPM commitment that ties capacity ramp milestones to invoice/disbursement triggers and term discounts. Goal here is to balance Aurora's need for a gradual onramp with Redwood's desire for predictable utilization and an economic prepay structure.

High-level proposal (3-year commitment):
- Year 1 ramp (milestone-based): Q1: 8 GPUs + 8 TPMs (onboard), Q2: +24 GPUs, Q3: +32 GPUs (full prod baseline) — total Year1 target: 64 GPUs.
- Year 2 add: 64 additional GPUs (scale to 128), Year 3 add: optional expansion tranche of 64 (customer optional).
- Pricing: Base unit price $X per GPU-hour equivalent (see attached proposal). Term discount: 12% on list for a signed 3-year agreement with annual prepay. If Aurora chooses annual invoiced (net30) rather than annual prepay, discount would be 8%.
- Milestone acceptance: Each quarter's ramp increase will be accepted once basic throughput and stability checks are met (uptime >= 99.5%, end-to-end latency within agreed SLOs). If acceptance is delayed, the next milestone payment is deferred until acceptance.
- True-up: Quarterly true-up with ability to shift up to 10% of next quarter's capacity within a year without penalty. True-ups beyond that are subject to pricing adjustment.
- Onboarding credits: 3 months of token/compute credits applied to first invoice to offset migration cost (reflected in proposal).
- Procurement: We can split Year1 prepay into two equal invoices (signing and mid-year) if that helps with Aurora's budget/PO cadence.

Attached is a redlined proposal (Aurora-Dedicated-Proposal-v3.pdf) and a draft SOW for the onboarding program. Happy to walk through line items on a quick call.

Next steps I suggest: 1) Confirm you can accept milestone-based ramp dates above (or propose adjustments), 2) confirm whether Aurora requires annual prepay vs annual invoice, and 3) we will produce a DocuSign-ready contract and final SOW.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0189

Attachments: Aurora-Dedicated-Proposal-v3.pdf (proposal + pricing grid), SOW-Aurora-Dedicated.docx (onboarding scope), SOC2-Summary.pdf (security snapshot)
From: Emily Park <emily@auroradata.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@auroradata.com
Date: 2026-04-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Milestone-tied commit schedule for dedicated capacity — Aurora Data

Jonas —

Thanks for the detailed proposal and attachments. High level this looks promising; a few items procurement/engineering asked me to clarify before we route to legal and finance: 

1) Ramp cadence: The Q1 8->32 jump in Q2 is aggressive for our SRE team given current internal integrations. Can we do a softer Q2 addition (e.g., Q1: 8, Q2: +16, Q3: +24) so our feature teams have room for staged validation?

2) Prepay vs invoice: Procurement prefers annual invoiced (net30) terms for this first year due to our internal PO flows. Would Redwood accept the 8% discount model you mentioned rather than requiring prepay?

3) True-up flex: Quarterly true-up with 10% shift is fine, but we need an option to push a one-time additional 10% into the following quarter without repricing if the increase is driven by a ramping pilot. Can we add that as an exception?

4) SLA credits: Engineering asked whether a higher initial uptime SLA (99.8%) is available for the production tranche (Q3 forward) or whether we can get a stronger SLA credit schedule.

5) Procurement requested a sample contract clause for milestone acceptance delays and invoice deferrals so they can assess approval risk.

If you can respond to the five points above and update the SOW/proposal, procurement will try to route a PO in our May window.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Park
Head of ML Infrastructure, Aurora Data
emily@auroradata.com
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-14T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Milestone-tied commit schedule for dedicated capacity — Aurora Data

Jonas / Ben —

I reviewed Emily's asks. Recommended negotiation posture and concessions below (keep it tight):

- Ramp cadence: Agree to a softened Year1 ramp to Q1:8, Q2:+16, Q3:+24 (total 48 in Year1). Offer a one-time discretionary pilot top-up of 10% of next quarter without repricing (to address their #3).
- Discount / payment: Accept Aurora's preference for annual invoiced net30 at an 8% discount for Year1. Offer tiered improvement: Year2 automatic 10% discount (subject to meeting min-utilization of 70% Y1) and Year3 12% if they convert to annual prepay at renewal. This keeps us flexible and gives Aurora a path to better economics.
- SLA: For Q3 production tranche, commit to 99.7% SLA with a more aggressive credit schedule in the first 12 months (first breach: service credit 5% of month invoice, second breach escalate). We can offer 99.8% but only if they accept 12% discount and annual prepay — probably too big a stretch.
- Milestone acceptance language: Provide contract clause that ties invoice trigger to acceptance tests (uptime/latency checks) but include a 30-day remediation window before deferral. Procurement usually likes that.
- PO cadence: Offer to split Year1 invoice into two (signing + mid-year) to help with PO flow.

If they accept the softened ramp and net30 8% discount, we should be comfortable. Ben, can you confirm numbers and margin impact so I can sign off?

— Lauren
VP Sales Operations
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Emily Park <emily@auroradata.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-15T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Milestone-tied commit schedule for dedicated capacity — Aurora Data

Emily —

Appreciate the clear feedback. Per our internal review we can accept the revised cadence and procurement terms with the following final counter-proposal: 

Final commercial summary (3-year commitment):
- Year1 ramp (accepted): Q1: 8 GPUs, Q2: +16, Q3: +24 (48 GPUs in Year1).
- One-time discretionary pilot top-up: Aurora may request a one-time additional 10% capacity for the immediately following quarter without repricing (must be requested 14 days before quarter start).
- Pricing & payment: Year1 discount 8% with annual invoiced (net30). Year2 discount 10% contingent on Year1 utilization >= 70% (quarterly measured), Year3 discount 12% if Aurora converts to annual prepay at renewal.
- SLA: Production tranche (from Q3) SLA 99.7% with an enhanced credit cadence in Year1 (first breach: 5% month credit, second breach escalate to CS/engineering). We can discuss laddering for 99.8% if they commit to prepay.
- Milestone acceptance & invoices: Invoice trigger tied to acceptance tests with a 30-day remediation window for remediation/retest. If acceptance fails after remediation, invoice is deferred until acceptance.
- Invoice split: We will split Year1 invoice into two equal invoices to accommodate PO timing (sign + mid-year).
- Onboarding credits: 3 months compute credit applied to the first invoice.

I attached an updated SOW and a redline of the acceptance clause (see SOW-Aurora-Dedicated.docx). For convenience here are the next steps we propose:
1) Redwood issues DocuSign contract with the commercial summary above.
2) Aurora routes PO for Year1 net30 invoiced terms.
3) Once PO received we schedule onboarding kickoff.

Link to proposal + DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/rdw/doc/aurora-dedicated-proposal

If that aligns with Aurora's procurement timelines we can target a May PO and June onboarding start. Let me know and I'll push the contract through.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Jonas / Lauren / Ben —

This looks good to us. Procurement will route an initial PO on the net30 annual invoice model with the softened ramp (Q1:8, Q2:+16, Q3:+24) and the one-time 10% pilot top-up option. We will also include the 30-day remediation window language in the PO routing notes.

thread_summary: Negotiation for a 3-year dedicated capacity commitment with milestone-tied ramp schedule; internal approval to accept softened Year1 ramp, net30 invoiced Year1 at 8% discount, tiered year-over-year discounts tied to utilization, SLA compromise, one-time pilot top-up, and invoice split to support PO cadence. Final agreement pending PO and DocuSign.
